newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers mainly steady, West Africa softens.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers mainly steady, West Africa softens.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates were mainly steady on Tuesday but West African cargoes continued to soften, brokers said.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf 130,000 tonne vessels were fixed at W100, five points lower, continuing Monday's slide after firming steadily last week.
"They're on the way down. Ships are returning (to West Africa) and stems have been filled for April. There should be no trouble fixing right now," one broker said.
However, there was good interest in West Africa/Asia cargoes, with 310,000 tonnes fixed on the Mare Champion at $1.1 million to India for Vitol, loading April 10.
Very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates were little changed, with several fixed from the Middle East to South Korea at around W64. Voyages west were steady at W55 and to Singapore at W62.5.
North Sea/transatlantic VLCCs were comparable with the West Africa market at W72.5/75, brokers said.
Cross-Med 80,000 tonners edged up to W110 as vessels slipped out of the region and also had to compete with good activity in the inter-U.K./cont sector.
"A lot of vessels have disappeared between yesterday and today. The market is definitely firmer than at the end of last week," an Italian broker said.
The inter-U.K./Cont sector remained firm with 80,000 tonnes fixed at up to W140, while 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were steady at W195.
However, Med fuel oil slipped to W205/210 from W220 on sagging demand, brokers said.
The upcoast/U.S. market maintained its strength, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W205/210 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil vessels at a similar level.
